title: The mock hiring test
intro:
This is the test the whole path has been building towards: **10 tasks in 45 minutes**, the way a practical Excel test for a junior analyst runs.

- **Part 1 (7 tasks)** uses the clean order log: conditional totals and counts, logic, and lookups in every direction. Type each answer as a formula.
- **Part 2 (3 tasks)** hands you the raw export: clean it, pivot it, chart it and write the sentence.

The clock starts when you press **Start** and doesn't stop, not even if you reload or close the tab. When it reaches zero, your answers are submitted as they are. You get **one submission per attempt**. The answer key appears after you submit, never before. **Pass: 8 of 10**, within the time.

There are two variants. Each retake uses the other one, so a second try tests the skills, not your memory of the answers. If you open a variant's key and later pass that same variant, the pass is recorded as *passed with help*.

pool.ask: Total **quantity** Sofia Papadaki sold through the **Field** channel.
pool.hint: Two conditions: rep and channel. SUMIFS puts the range to add first.

pool.ask: Total **quantity** of **P012** (Toner Cartridge) sold in **Attica**.
pool.hint: Two conditions: product and region. SUMIFS puts the range to add first.

pool.ask: How many **Partner** orders had a quantity of **10 or more**?
pool.hint: "10 or more" includes 10: the criterion is ">=10", in quotes.

pool.ask: How many **Online** orders came from **Macedonia**?
pool.hint: Count rows where both conditions hold.

pool.ask: The average **quantity per Attica order**, rounded to **1 decimal place**.
pool.hint: Attica's units ÷ Attica's orders, wrapped in ROUND(…,1).

pool.ask: Did Thessaly sell **at least 250 units** in total? Return **"Yes"** or **"No"**.
pool.hint: Units means the Quantity column, summed; not the number of orders.

pool.ask: The **Category** of the product in order **O1033** (row 34). Lock the product table.
pool.hint: Category is the 3rd column of J:N. End with FALSE.

pool.ask: The **ListPrice** of the product in order **O1077** (row 78). Lock the product table.
pool.hint: ListPrice is the 5th column of J:N; UnitCost is the 4th. End with FALSE.

pool.ask: The discount **Band** for order **O1146**'s quantity (row 147), from the Tiers table.
pool.hint: Tiers are bands, so this is an approximate match (TRUE): the largest MinQty ≤ the quantity.

pool.ask: The discount **Band** for order **O1169**'s quantity (row 170), from the Tiers table.
pool.hint: Tiers are bands, so this is an approximate match (TRUE): the largest MinQty ≤ the quantity.

pool.ask: The **RepID** of the rep on order **O1150** (row 151). The Reps table has RepID to the *left* of RepName.
pool.hint: Search RepName (Q), return RepID (P): INDEX/MATCH with 0, or XLOOKUP.

pool.ask: The **ProductID** of **Headset Pro**. ProductID is to the *left* of ProductName.
pool.hint: Search ProductName (K), return ProductID (J): INDEX/MATCH with 0, or XLOOKUP.

pool.ask: The **margin** on order **O1060** (row 61): revenue after discount, minus quantity × UnitCost.
pool.hint: Revenue = Quantity × ListPrice × (1 − Discount); then subtract Quantity × UnitCost.

pool.ask: The **revenue** of order **O1141** (row 142), showing **0** if its product isn't in the price list.
pool.hint: Wrap the whole revenue formula in IFERROR(…, 0).

pool.ask: **Clean, part 1:** remove the duplicated orders and fill the blank regions (from each order's rep).
pool.hint: Remove Duplicates (every column); then fill only the blank Regions with a lookup of the rep's name in Q:R.

pool.ask: **Clean, part 2:** standardise the region names, make every quantity a number, and fix the mistyped ProductID and the date in the wrong year.

pool.ask: **Pivot and slide:** total **Margin by Category** on the cleaned data (no % view), charted so the top category stands out, with a finding title and the sentence completed.
pool.hint: Rows: Category; Values: Sum of Margin; refreshed after cleaning. Columns or bars, largest first; the title names the top category.

pool.ask: **Pivot and slide:** total **Revenue by Rep** on the cleaned data (no % view), charted so the top rep stands out, with a finding title and the sentence completed.
pool.hint: Rows: Rep; Values: Sum of Revenue; refreshed after cleaning. Columns or bars, largest first; the title names the top rep.
